Both Sprint 5 design docs now have real, dedicated review history. dpdp-crypto-shredding-full-erasure-design.md is v2.3, having been through 13 solution-architect rounds AND a separate 4-round consensus-agent failure-mode/retry/rollback/escalation review, both ending in a clean APPROVE for DASH-STORY-027 with no outstanding findings. connection-pooling-design.md is now v2.6, having been through its own dedicated 2-round adversarial solution-architect review (round 1 found a real defect -- the doc's claimed migration mechanism didn't match how src/dashanan/api/composition.py and app.py actually construct repositories today, and Zone 8's manifest/consolidation/archiver/erasure-service classes were entirely missing from scope; round 2 verified the fix and found 2 further issues -- a scrambled zone-number/repository-name pairing and an understated DASH-STORY-028 story-point estimate -- both fixed) plus a follow-on consensus-agent failure-mode review that found DASH-STORY-028's expanded scope lacked a disclosed rollback path and clear retry granularity -- both fixed, bumping to v2.2. Neither doc is marked IMPLEMENTATION-READY in its own Status line yet (that requires also clearing a real dispatched Phase C gate, which has not run for either), but both have now had genuine adversarial review depth, not a single authoring pass. This sprint plan and the Phase 7 routing bundle that follows it are therefore honestly scoped as PRE-IMPLEMENTATION-READY planning, not yet a Phase-C-gate-hardened bundle ready for Phase B dispatch -- see sprint5-ar5-rs-computation.md's Verdict for the explicit gating consequence of this.

None of these block the design from being a coherent, internally-consistent proposal, but they are real gaps a future review round should close before this story is scored implementation-ready.
